text: Certain parties urge that we expand the geographic limits of the section 202(c) exemption but continue to determine the scope of the section 203(b)(8) exemption by reference to existing regulations. The argument is that this would result in substantial benefits to both shippers and carriers with less disruption to the existing regulatory scheme. Initially, we note that we have a legislative mandate to exempt local operations in conformity with the meaning of section 203(b)(8). We have found that the geographic scope of those local operations now extends into suburban areas beyond the limits of the original population-mileage formula. On the basis of the evidence before us, we do not find it necessary to withhold the updating of zone limits for policy reasons. Shipper representations in this proceeding indicate that local cartage operations within existing commercial zone limits is of acceptable quality. No concrete evidence to the contrary was submitted. Nor have we encountered any complaints relating to abuses of destructive competition in areas where the commercial zone limits have been expanded through individual determinations. We have also noted in earlier sections of this report certain administrative and functional benefits of uniform expansion of commercial zones and terminal areas. Furthermore, we believe that expansion of the geographic scope of the section 203(b)(8) exemption will introduce a measure of equality to the treatment of local operations in and around cities of similar size.
